gaps.sentence: Not ___ candidates applied for the position.
gaps.explanation: 'Not many' is used with countable plurals like candidates; 'not much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.

gaps.sentence: How ___ eggs do we need for the cake?
gaps.explanation: 'Eggs' is countable and plural, so 'how many' is used.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.
There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.
